segments.speaker: Bria Dixon
segments.text: Bria Dixon, Development Coordination. Agenda item 2 is rez 26-83, request to rezone 2423 East Ida Street from RS 50 residential single-family to Planned Development, Place of Religious Assembly. I will now turn it over to Planning Commission staff.

segments.speaker: Alan Clendenin
segments.text: Hold on one second. Sir, do you have a question? Go ahead. This is rez 26-83. It is located in the central Tampa Planning district. The East Tampa urban village. The East Tampa one neighborhood and evacuation zone e. The subject site is located here outlined in purple. The surrounding area is a mix of uses with single-family detached to the north, east, and west of the subject site. And along West Dr. Martin Luther King jr. boulevard are commercial uses as well as memorial park cemetery and cypress green park. The subject site is located here outlined in purple, represented with the residential 20 designation, which is to the north, east, and west of the subject site. The community commercial 35 designation is along Martin Luther King jr. boulevard. The site is currently occupied with an existing Place of Religious Assembly. This PD retains the existing use and proposes a new building on the site. The comprehensive plan promotes pedestrian safety and encourages development that enhances the city's character and ambience by encouraging a pedestrian friendly environment and connection to surrounding uses. The PD addresses these policies by providing five foot sidewalks along the rights-of-way and bicycle parking. Off-site parking will also serve this site. The front entrance is oriented towards east Ida Street and a connection is provided to the sidewalk. If approved, Planning Commission staff requests that a sidewalk connection from the side entry to the existing sidewalk on north 26th street be added between first and second readings. The comprehensive plan also encourages nonresidential development to be appropriately buffered and screened from adjacent residential uses. The site abuts single-family residential to the west and south. The landscape buffer to the single-family residences to the west and south of the site are 10 feet while the building setback is 15 feet to the south and 20 feet to the west consistent with this policy direction. Overall, the request is compatible and consistent with the development pattern anticipated under the residential 20 designation. That concludes my presentation, if you have any questions.

segments.speaker: Alan Clendenin
segments.text: Thank you, any questions? Hearing none.

segments.speaker: Bria Dixon
segments.text: Bria Dixon, Development Coordination. We'll start with an aerial view of the subject property. The subject property is outlined here in red. It is located just of east South Ida Street and just west of north 26th street and also east of north 24th street here. The subject property is currently developed with a Place of Religious Assembly or a church. Surrounding uses are primarily RS 50 to the north as well as to the west. To the east is a Planned Development for residential multiple family development. It has not yet been developed and is currently still developed with a single-family detached residence, and to the south in a CI zoning designation, there is a vehicle sales and leasing. I have a site plan as provided by the applicant. Here on the site plan, you can see that to the north is -- to the north is east ida. To the east is north 26th street. The applicant is proposing a Place of Religious Assembly here. The entrance is going to be here from east ida. The site is currently located -- is not located on the collector or interior street and is on a lot less than 20,000 square feet. No off-street parking is proposed, and there is an existing five-foot sidewalk here along north 26 that the applicant is proposing to continue here on east ida. In 2000 the property received a special use approval for a Place of Religious Assembly. Under the current approval the property appears to be developed as is under the approval. The current application request to rezone the property to allow the installation of a new 2,200-square-foot facility, which is here. It's going to be a prefabricated building utilized once again as a church. The applicant is requesting waivers to allow reduced setbacks on the west, south and east as well as the north. For the purposes of constructing a tree outside of the protected root zones, here you can see trees to the north as well as here, and then further there are trees here in the alley, protective root zones are outlined in these light dashed lines. Due to the limited size of the subject property and the careful consideration of the natural elements on-site, staff supports the waiver request. Here are the elevations. You have north, south, west, and east. And the applicant is requesting six waivers. One from section 27-132 to reduce the required -- rear yard from 40 feet to 50. Anterior side yard from 40 feet to 10, corner side yard from 40 feet to 5. Section 27-132 reduce required minimum lot size from 20,000 square feet for nonresidential use to 7,125 square feet for 64% reduction. From section 27-132 to allow vehicle access from local streets, east ida and north 26 in lieu of the required access to an arterial or collector street. Section 27-240, which is the overlay, request to allow a 15-foot setback from the front facade instead of the required 10 to 12-foot range. A second request from the overlay section 27-240 to reduce the required sidewalk width pursuant to East Tampa overlay from the required six to the required five again to match that existing sidewalk on east 26th street. And there is another waiver finding number 6 to reduce the required number of parking spaces from 17 to 0. The development review and compliance staff has reviewed the petition and finds it inconsistent with the applicable City of Tampa land development regulations. Please refer to transportation, stormwater and Development Coordination comments for overall inconsistency finding. If City Council approves the application and waivers requested, modifications to the site plan shown on the submitted revision sheet must be completed between first and second reading. Revisions will not resolve transportation's finding of inconsistent. I'm available if there are any questions.

segments.speaker: Bria Dixon
segments.text: Yes. Sorry, council, I have photos showing the subject property here. This is the subject property from east ida, from north 26th. This is the vacant parcel across the street to the north. This is the Planned Development proposed on the east, currently single-family detached. Vehicle sales and leasing to the south and CI zoning. And then the single-family detached residence to the west. Presently, there are two parking spaces at the subject property.

segments.text: So there's two parking spaces currently right now?

segments.text: Emily Phelan, Planning Commission staff. We're asking for a sidewalk connection right here because currently it looks like there's like a concrete pad right outside the door, so we're just asking for it to continue to that sidewalk and have an extra connection.

segments.speaker: Alan Clendenin
segments.text: Thank you. Any other questions? Hearing none, applicant? Good evening, sir, if you would start with your name, please. My name is Pastor Thomas. I am the pastor of the grace of god missionary baptist church, but I also worked along with the contractor as the project manager on bringing this contract to this particular floor. I am just standing for you asking for your blessings as well as your approval on building this church. We've been in this area now for over 20 years. And the reason why we are rebuilding this church is because the two hurricanes has damaged the church existing very badly. So we are trying to build a new church in its place. As you can see from the drawings where that we do not want to encroach into any existing trees or any existing alleyway that's in the back. As a matter of fact, the grace of god has been taking care of that alley way and around that church for the last ten years. Most of all, more than anything else, church building itself is not going to be built like a warehouse. It will be decorated and designed as a church. It's going to be acceptable in the community. We will have -- you will see central lighting where I have a central light there, and lighting will be on all four parts of the building where that particular corner will be lit up and cameras will be there for security. Now, in one part of the waiver, we had zero parking, but when I went to development review, I was trying to get it where I could park in the right-of-way, but one of the people in rezoning said, what if you get with the school that's right adjacent to you, lomax. I got with the principal, and I have a letter from the principal and the staff saying they will grant me to use the parking space, but I have to get with the School Board and let them know of the date once I get the church built where we can rent and get a lease where that no cars will be parked in the right-of-way or in front of anybody residence where we will park in the parking spaces adjacent to lomax where we will be in their parking spaces, leasing it, cars in a private parking area secured where we will have it secured and have security there. We will actually put two cones on ida and two cones on 26th street where we would monitor the traffic going through there in doing that. So we want to make sure that we accommodate that area, and we've been taking care of that area and that surrounding area for the last 20 years. We will work with the permitting department on every end. And the reason why we wanted to reduce the sidewalk from six feet to five feet, you got an existing five foot sidewalk, like she said, on 26th street. Besides me being a pastor, just going -- I was a project engineer and I designed roadways and bridges for Hillsborough county. We normally match existing with existing. And why should I tear out an existing foot of already five foot sidewalk where I can match it because we're going into some drainage areas on the corner of 26th and ida, where you have a ditch bottom inlet and then you have two type throat inlets at the corner where it will cause a drainage problem, but at the same time, when I put the new five-foot sidewalk on ida, we are going to put penetrated type material, where we do not want to disturb the roots of those live oaks because I worked in park and recreation, and I do believe in saving trees instead of tearing them down. I got about nine trees in that area surrounding my church. The largest is a 42. The smallest around a 32. And we have 10-foot radiuses around them. Show that we're building a church to protect the trees, and we are putting down material where it will not damage the roots. The proposed sidewalk that you see, entryway egress going to the church, we will build certain materials where we'll have to demo the existing driveway by hand, remove the existing material, and come back and put new material in, in order to save the trees. And then we will work with the City of Tampa to get an arborist on trying to, I'll say, cut back the overlay of those trees so we could put the church in. So in other words, council members, trying to not bother you or bore you, we are here as a church to work with the city to keep those existing trees because people do not know oak trees are protected by the state and it helps keep the atmosphere clean. I'm a firm believer in that. As a matter of fact, when we do the demo of that existing building, we told the permitting department that we are willing to have an arborist come in there and we want to check the trees and see if the trees are ill, okay, because we have termites around there, and those trees are over a hundred years old. So we want to make sure that we protect those trees and at the same time build a church where we can be in the surrounding community to help them out.

segments.speaker: Alan Clendenin
segments.text: Thank you very much. I appreciate it. Thank you for listening to me.

If you're able to get this agreement with the school, I think that would be -- that would kind of set some of the ease, especially for me with the parking.

segments.speaker: Alan Clendenin
segments.text: There's only two spots now. Your congregation generally is walking I'm assuming? Been there, we had parking, and we come in and we come out. So all I have been doing from the beginning is working with the City of Tampa on trying to get a church built. Parking was one of my main designs from the beginning, okay, but I had to accommodate the new law of the 20,000 and how to pull in and to pull out. So we just went along with it. Only thing I'm saying is that I will follow along with you all, because I want to cooperate in every manner on trying to get this thing done, but I want to do it under the new law.

segments.text: I want to make sure I'm understanding the existing circumstances. Honestly, I'm not getting hung up on the parking issue.
